benchmark_scope.denominator_note: Three strategic corridors and one workbook-driven identity target; not four established open gates.
limits: Declared formal entry status and actual movement can diverge; neither derives from OSM.
Mandera/Liboi published map points are approximate references with unknown measurement quality.
Country pair must be checked independently around the Mandera tripoint; Doolow is out of scope.

sources.title: CS Duale leads high-profile delegation seeking to reopen Kenya-Somalia border
claims: Names Mandera–Bulahawa, Liboi–Dhobley and Kiunga–Ras Kamboni as three strategic crossings in the reopening talks.
Planned reopening and porous-border movement are distinguished from formal closure; this is not evidence that reopening occurred.

sources.title: Gazetted Ports of Entry and Exit (PoEs) and Location
claims: Lists Mandera, Liboi and Kiunga under the Somalia frontier as land entries, each marked closed.
sources.date_basis: Undated directory; no per-point observation date or assurance of current operations.

sources.title: Proposed PoEs
claims: Lists Elwak as a proposed land entry on the Somalia frontier, in Mandera County.
sources.date_basis: Undated directory; proposed status is preserved, not promoted to a currently operating formal gate.

sources.title: Terms of Reference for Rhamu and Mandera OSBPs and KRA accommodation
claims: Page 2 distinguishes Mandera as a Somalia crossing from Rhamu on the Ethiopia frontier; describes an existing gazetted Mandera station and proposed OSBP development.

sources.title: Isiolo–Modogashe–Wajir–Elwak–Rhamu–Mandera (A13)
claims: Identifies A13 as the approach corridor through Elwak and Mandera. It does not identify the final international gate spur or prove that A13 itself crosses the frontier.

sources.title: Horn of Africa Gateway Development Project: Madogo–Garissa–Dadaab–Liboi–Harhar A3 road
claims: Defines the A3 corridor to Liboi/Harhar border-post town. Describes unpaved/earth-road conditions in 2021, showing national-road importance is not equivalent to paved width.
sources.date_basis: Tender KeNHA/2414/2021; no current road-condition assertion.

sources.title: Somalia closes common border with Kenya to rein in coronavirus cases
claims: Reports Gedo authorities naming Balad-Hawo and Elwak as Kenya–Somalia entries, and separately Doolow as the Ethiopia entry.
sources.source_type: Original reporting of governor statement; used for workbook identity and country-pair distinction, not independent coordinate evidence.

sources.title: KRA Financial Statements FY 2019–2020
claims: Lists an Elwak land allocation for a proposed OSBP. Institutional designation/project status does not establish present operation.
sources.date_basis: Financial year end; publication date not established.

sources.title: One-Stop Border Post (OSBP) Status Report
claims: Appendix A gives Liboi E38 [longitude 40.99437, latitude 0.40898] and Mandera E40 [41.85729, 3.96209].
These illustrative map-legend points have no documented accuracy, datum, collection date or independence from OSM.
sources.date_basis: Report published among PIDA Week 2024 resources; PDF creation metadata 2024-11-05 does not establish point observation dates.
sources.access: Full 84-page PDF downloaded; Appendix A extracted locally and corroborated by indexed source text.
sources.locator: Appendix A, printed page 79 / PDF page 81, E38 and E40

sources.title: Somalia: Security Situation — 2.1.1. Gedo
claims: The Gedo background section identifies Ceel Waaq as also written El Waq/El Wak, and Belet Xaawo as Bulo Hawa.
Used only for place-name reconciliation; does not identify an exact gate coordinate, current opening status or historical closure scope.

sources.title: Elwak Municipality Integrated Development Plan 2022–2026
sources.publisher: Elwak Municipality / County Government of Mandera; hosted by Mandera County Assembly
sources.date_basis: Cover month; upload path says February2026, which is not the document date.
claims: Printed page 3 (PDF page 16) locates El-Wak town at 2°48′34″N, 40°56′9″E and describes its Kenya–Somalia border setting.
The coordinate is a town reference, not a surveyed border gate; it supports regional identity only.

sources.title: Deris Wanaag: The Kenya-Somalia-Ethiopia Borderlands Project
sources.date_basis: Undated project page; retrieved version describes 2023–2026 research.
claims: The institution’s own research project names the Kiunga–Ishakani–Ras Kamboni cross-border area.
This is a regional identity source; it does not establish a gate coordinate or current vehicle access.
